principle: Framework hooks show what the agent attempted. Authority, resource, lifecycle, supervision, and evidence surfaces establish whether control actually held.

surfaces.name: Action driver
surfaces.question: How does Asimov exercise the real agent or tool path?
surfaces.warning: Do not substitute a synthetic test-only path for the production route you are claiming.

surfaces.name: Authority controller
surfaces.question: What real mechanism grants, bounds, expires, and revokes consequential authority?
surfaces.warning: Prompts, role descriptions, and framework-level allowlists are not automatically enforceable authority boundaries.

surfaces.name: Resource truth
surfaces.question: What authoritative source tells Asimov what actually happened?
surfaces.warning: Agent text, framework traces, and orchestration state are not proof of an external effect.

surfaces.name: Lifecycle
surfaces.question: What can safely restart, partition, stop, or fault the deployed system?
surfaces.warning: A UI pause or cooperative agent stop is not the same as infrastructure-level lifecycle control.

surfaces.name: Supervision
surfaces.question: What authenticated intervention path remains outside the actor's effective authority?
surfaces.warning: A supervisor running with the same unrestricted privileges as the actor is not independent.

surfaces.name: Evidence
surfaces.question: What records can reconstruct requests, decisions, effects, failures, and control changes?
surfaces.warning: Preserve disagreements between orchestration logs and resource-side evidence rather than hiding them.

runtime_options.name: OpenAI Agents API
runtime_options.summary: OpenAI runs the managed agent harness and durable session/orchestration layer; your application still owns surrounding integrations and chooses where tool execution occurs.
not_enough: Agents API event history alone does not prove the destination resource changed.
Provider-hosted execution must be treated as a real action path, not hidden behind one application callback.

recommended.action: Create and steer real Agents API sessions through the same application route used in production.
recommended.authority: Bind consequential tools to external IAM, a policy gateway, or resource-side authorization; keep application/API credentials outside agent-controlled sandboxes.
recommended.resource: Read the protected database/API/cloud resource independently.
recommended.lifecycle: Use the selected environment/sandbox controls plus the application's hosting control plane.
recommended.supervision: Keep A3+ intervention in an external operator/policy/infrastructure path.
recommended.evidence: Combine Agents API events with application integration logs and resource/provider audit.

runtime_options.note: OpenAI recommends the Agents API for new agent applications as of this catalog check.

runtime_options.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
runtime_options.summary: The agent loop runs in your application; your server owns deployment, tool implementations, storage, and approval decisions.
runtime_options.action_driver: Agents SDK runner / application entry point
not_enough: SDK traces do not prove the external effect.
A tool guardrail or application callback is not automatically an authority boundary if the actor can bypass it through another route.

recommended.action: Run the same SDK Runner/tool path used by production.
recommended.authority: Place real authorization outside model-written instructions and preferably outside the agent process for higher profiles.
recommended.resource: Use the target DB/API/filesystem/cloud service as the oracle.
recommended.supervision: Use a separate supervisor or policy/infrastructure service for A3+.
recommended.evidence: Pair SDK tracing with resource-side and authority-side evidence.

runtime_options.note: The Agents SDK is feature-complete and maintained; OpenAI recommends Agents API for new applications.

runtime_options.name: OpenAI Responses API / custom loop
runtime_options.summary: You own the application logic and any agent loop around Responses while OpenAI provides model responses and configured hosted capabilities.
not_enough: Model/tool-call output is not evidence that an external action succeeded.
Hosted tools and client-executed tools may have different trust boundaries.

recommended.authority: Use external authorization for client tools and explicit provider controls for hosted capabilities.
recommended.lifecycle: Use your application/hosting lifecycle plus any hosted environment lifecycle you depend on.
recommended.supervision: Put high-consequence intervention outside the model loop.
recommended.evidence: Correlate response/tool events with resource and authorization logs.

runtime_options.name: Claude Managed Agents
runtime_options.summary: Anthropic hosts the agent harness and can host the execution environment; sessions are stateful and may use built-in tools, sandboxes, or MCP connections.
not_enough: Session events alone do not establish resource truth.
Built-in or hosted tools are distinct provider-side action paths that need matching evidence.

recommended.action: Create and steer real managed sessions.
recommended.authority: Use environment/tool policies plus external resource/IAM controls; do not rely on the agent configuration as the sole security boundary.
recommended.lifecycle: Use Managed Agent environment/session controls and the hosting control plane for any self-hosted environment.
recommended.supervision: Use an operator/policy path outside the agent session for A3+.
recommended.evidence: Combine session events with resource, IAM, and environment logs.

runtime_options.name: Claude Agent SDK
runtime_options.summary: Anthropic's agent harness runs in a process you operate, so the application owns the runtime and local tool execution boundary.
not_enough: Hooks executing inside the same unrestricted process are not independent enforcement.
SDK tool success text is not resource-side proof.

recommended.action: Exercise the real SDK session and tool path.
recommended.authority: Back permissions with OS/cloud/resource controls for consequential effects.
recommended.supervision: Keep the only stop/restrict path outside generated-code privileges.
recommended.evidence: Combine SDK hooks/events with authoritative resource and IAM logs.

runtime_options.name: Claude Messages API / custom loop
runtime_options.summary: You write the agent loop and execute client tools; server tools execute on Anthropic's side.
not_enough: Client and server tools have different execution boundaries.
The model's tool request or returned text does not establish that an effect occurred.

recommended.authority: Apply resource/IAM or policy-gateway controls before consequential client execution.
recommended.supervision: Use an out-of-band operator/policy path for A3+.
recommended.evidence: Preserve message/tool records plus external resource/audit records.

runtime_options.name: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
runtime_options.summary: ADK can run locally or on Google-hosted runtimes; agent, model, tool, session, and callback surfaces provide orchestration hooks while cloud identity and resources provide stronger boundaries.
runtime_options.action_driver: ADK runner/workflow or deployed agent endpoint
useful_hooks: Agent Runtime or Cloud Run/GKE deployment hooks
not_enough: Callbacks are orchestration hooks, not automatically independent control.
Session state is not proof of external resource effects.

recommended.action: Use the real ADK runner or deployed endpoint.
recommended.authority: Use service accounts/workload identity and resource IAM.
recommended.resource: Read Google Cloud or application resource state independently.
recommended.lifecycle: Use Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, GKE, or local process controls as deployed.
recommended.supervision: Use cloud/operator control outside the agent's service identity.
recommended.evidence: Combine ADK events/traces with Cloud Audit Logs and resource truth.

runtime_options.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
runtime_options.summary: Agent Framework supports agents, workflows, harness agents, middleware, sessions, and multiple hosting models; integrations may be application-owned or remote.
runtime_options.action_driver: Agent run, workflow execution, or harness-agent entry point
not_enough: Middleware running with actor-equivalent authority is not an independent enforcement boundary.
Workflow state does not establish external resource truth.

recommended.action: Exercise the same Agent Framework agent/workflow/harness route used in production.
recommended.authority: Use Entra/RBAC, workload identity, resource authorization, or a separate policy layer.
recommended.lifecycle: Use the selected self-hosted/Azure Functions/durable hosting control plane.
recommended.supervision: Use authenticated operator/governance controls outside actor authority.
recommended.evidence: Combine framework events/checkpoints with Azure/resource audit.

runtime_options.name: LangGraph / LangChain agents
runtime_options.summary: Graph execution, checkpoints, interrupts, and deployment runtimes provide durable orchestration surfaces; the protected resource remains the authoritative effect oracle.
runtime_options.action_driver: Graph invocation / agent run / tool node
not_enough: A checkpoint proves orchestration state, not the external effect.
Human-in-the-loop interrupts are not a substitute for resource-side authorization if the actor can bypass the interrupted path.

recommended.authority: Use IAM/policy gateway/resource authorization outside graph state.
recommended.lifecycle: Use LangSmith Deployment, Kubernetes, process, or cloud lifecycle controls as applicable.
recommended.supervision: Use a supervisor/policy path outside the acting principal.
recommended.evidence: Combine graph/checkpoint/run events with authoritative resource evidence.

runtime_options.name: CrewAI
runtime_options.summary: CrewAI combines agents, crews, and flows; flows can provide the surrounding state/control workflow while crews perform delegated agent work.
not_enough: Agent roles and names are descriptive, not authenticated security identities.
Flow or crew state does not prove a protected resource changed.

recommended.authority: Bind tools to external IAM/policy/resource controls.
recommended.supervision: Keep intervention outside the crew's own model/tool authority.
recommended.evidence: Combine flow/crew telemetry with resource-side audit.

runtime_options.name: Custom / local open-weight stack
runtime_options.summary: Custom Python, Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, and similar stacks give you direct control, but Asimov still requires separation between actor, authority, observation, and supervision for higher assurance.
runtime_options.action_driver: Your orchestrator / model server / tool dispatcher
not_enough: Owning every component does not make them independent.
A single unrestricted process cannot credibly be both actor and sole A3+ supervisor.

recommended.authority: Use OS identities, a policy service, short-lived credentials, or resource authorization.
recommended.resource: Inspect files/DB/API/service state from a separate identity/process where possible.
recommended.supervision: Use a separate process/service or OS/infrastructure boundary.
recommended.evidence: Combine local runtime events with resource and OS/service audit.

integration_options.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
integration_options.summary: Treat every connected MCP server/tool family as part of the consequential action surface. MCP is a transport/integration boundary, not one universal security boundary.
integration_options.warning: Do not collapse all MCP tools into a single 'MCP' capability or assume the client can independently prove what a server did.

hosting_options.name: Local process / workstation
hosting_options.warning: Use a separate process/identity for independent supervision where the profile requires it.

hosting_options.name: Docker / single-host containers
hosting_options.warning: Do not give the actor Docker-socket authority if container isolation is part of the claimed boundary.

hosting_options.name: Kubernetes
hosting_options.warning: Use workload identity and exercise restart, partition, and common-mode dependencies for higher profiles.

hosting_options.name: AWS
hosting_options.warning: Measure revocation at the protected resource, not merely at IAM API acknowledgement.

hosting_options.name: Microsoft Azure
hosting_options.warning: Managed identity and token lifetime/propagation belong in revocation semantics.

hosting_options.name: Google Cloud
hosting_options.lifecycle: Google Cloud hosting / Agent Runtime / GKE / Cloud Run
hosting_options.warning: Service-account and resource-policy propagation belong in revocation semantics.

authority_options.name: AWS IAM / STS
authority_options.hint: roles, session/resource policies, short-lived credentials, explicit deny

authority_options.name: Microsoft Entra ID / Azure RBAC
authority_options.hint: managed identities, RBAC, resource policies, Key Vault or equivalent

authority_options.name: Google Cloud IAM
authority_options.hint: service accounts, workload identity, resource IAM, short-lived credentials

authority_options.name: External policy / authorization gateway
authority_options.hint: central admission/revocation outside the acting principal

authority_options.name: OS identity / ACL / service account
authority_options.hint: process identities, filesystem/service permissions, job/service boundaries

authority_options.name: Application authorization service
authority_options.hint: use only when it is enforceable and not bypassable by alternate actor routes

resource_options.name: PostgreSQL / SQL database
resource_options.oracle: separate read/audit identity; authoritative row/event/audit state

resource_options.name: HTTP / SaaS API
resource_options.oracle: authoritative GET/state endpoint or server-side audit

resource_options.name: Filesystem
resource_options.oracle: separate process/identity or disposable externally inspected workspace

resource_options.name: Queue / background jobs
resource_options.oracle: enqueue, admission, execution, cancellation, retry, and orphan state

resource_options.name: Cloud control-plane resource
resource_options.oracle: provider API/resource state plus cloud audit

resource_options.name: Other protected resource
resource_options.oracle: define a source of truth independent of the actor's own narrative

evidence_options.name: OpenTelemetry
evidence_options.role: correlated runtime events; not sole proof of external effects

evidence_options.name: Resource-native audit
evidence_options.role: effect truth at the protected system

evidence_options.name: Application/framework events
evidence_options.role: proposal, dispatch, orchestration, and lifecycle context
